Claim amended · 2026-11-02T12:12Z · phase 1 measured (run record `/mnt/project-files/issue-29117/phase1-run-record.md`, `main` `f2bf2938`); phase 2 opens. Branch, session and size are unchanged.

Clause-②: no
Metadata-protocol: none

- **Measured: the two clocks differ.** Workspace Pacific/Auckland, browser America/New_York, real clock 12:00Z (NY 11-02, Auckland 11-03), `closed_won` rows on 11-02 and 11-03: the authored list-view filter `close_date between [{today},{today}]` was sent resolved as `["2026-11-02","2026-11-02"]` (1 row, 11-02); the reader's panel filter was sent as `["{today}","{today}"]` and the server answered 1 row (11-03); both on one view sent both days and drew 0 rows. The reverse pair flips; same-zone controls agree. The page already had the zone (`/auth/me/localization` answered Auckland); `resolveDateMacros` never reads one. Every other client caller of `resolveDateMacros` (useResolvedFilter family, ObjectDataPage URL filters, grid, plugin-view, charts, dashboard widgets, compare-to, calendar initialDate) uses the browser clock by reading.
- **Ruling (seat):** the workspace timezone decides, as the console's timezone prompt promises and as the server already resolves. `resolveDateMacros` resolves calendar tokens (`today`, week/month/quarter/year bounds, `N_days/weeks/months/years`) on the wall clock of `@object-ui/core`'s `getDisplayTimeZone()` (set by `LocalizationProvider` from the same `localization.timezone` cascade); instant tokens (`now`, `N_minutes/hours`) stay on the real instant; no zone known ⇒ the browser clock, as today. No signature change, so Clause-② stays `no`; an explicit `timeZone` parameter is not taken.
- **File surface (phase 2):** `ui/packages/core/src/utils/date-macros.ts` and its tests; `ui/packages/app-shell/src/views/objectViewListRenderer.tsx` (the authored-filter `substituteFilterTokens` call only: read `useLocalization().timezone` so the filter re-resolves when the zone lands); a root `.changeset` (`@object-ui/core`, `@object-ui/app-shell` patch). Not `filter-tokens.ts`, not the other callers (they gain the fix through `resolveDateMacros`; their re-resolve-on-zone-arrival is out of scope and named in the PR). Stop on breach.
- **Serial constraints cleared:** PR #29266 (#28950) on `objectViewListRenderer.tsx` has landed; PR #29263 (#29115, seat 3) owns `filter-builder.tsx`/`filterRelativeDates.ts`, disjoint (phase 1 overlaid them in Vite only, restored).
